subject: SLO bucketization + fallback playbook — post-call notes
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@tidewell.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO bucketization + fallback playbook — post-call notes

Hi Priya — thanks again for your time today. Recap below from our discovery call and the mutual action items we agreed on. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

High-level pain points (as we heard them)
- 99th percentile latency spikes during batch imports and periodic peak traffic windows (payroll cut windows).
- Throughput variability: bursts to ~120 qps during peak, idle median ~8 qps.
- Model fidelity concerns for short-form customer messages vs. long-context policy docs (two distinct inference profiles).
- Tight security/compliance constraints (audit logs + regional data residency).

Goals you called out
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 150ms for short prompts (<= 200 tokens).
- Target p99: <= 600ms under sustained peak (120 qps) with graceful degradation beyond that.
- Cost sensitivity: reduce per-1M-token spend vs current provider by ~25–35% or justify with reliability.

Technical notes / constraints we captured
- Typical prompt length distribution: 60% <= 150 tokens; 30% 150–800 tokens; 10% >800 tokens.
- KV/cache friendliness for templated replies and session state — we discussed prefix caching.
- You run in us-west region with strict egress rules to your VPC.

Recommended immediate approach (short of full POC)
1) SLO bucketization: separate short-prompt cohort (<=200 tokens) from long-context cohort and route to different model profiles.
2) Primary model: mid-sized open model quantized for cost (we suggested Redwood-quant-v2), fallback to a lower-cost causal variant for extreme load.
3) Autoscale + reserved capacity for scheduled import windows; pre-warm KV cache before payroll windows.
4) Observability: token-level tracing and per-route p50/p95/p99 dashboards; we will grant a demo telemetry stream for a week.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-topology.pdf (illustrative topology + routing policy) and kv-cache-estimates.xlsx (estimate of cache hit impact on tokens).

Mutual action plan (dates)
- By Wed 2028-02-28: Tidewell to share 7-day sample traffic + prompt-length histogram and a sanitized example prompt set (we discussed anonymized customer messages).
- By Fri 2028-03-03: Redwood to provide an initial cost/latency estimate and a proposed canary config for short-prompt cohort.
- Week of 2028-03-06: Technical deep-dive (1hr) with your infra team for VPC and routing details.

Next steps: Priya — can you confirm the data sample deliverable and if 2028-03-08 for the deep-dive works for your team?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya@tidewell.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO bucketization + fallback playbook — post-call notes

Jordan — thank you for the thorough capture. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

1) Latency targets: the p95 <=150ms you captured is what our product org wants for conversational snippets. For p99, 600ms is acceptable as a hard requirement during normal operations; if you can meet p99 <=400ms for the short cohort we would be delighted.
2) Throughput: peak bursts can hit up to 140 qps for short prompts during campaign sends, not just 120. Sustained peaks last ~6–12 minutes.
3) Model fidelity: we need better hallucination controls for policy doc summarization — those fall into the long-context cohort.

We will deliver: a 7-day anonymized sample with token histograms and ~300 sanitized prompt examples by Tue 2028-02-28 EOD (I’ll send a link to the secure S3 bucket). We’ll also include our current provider’s p95/p99 traces for a 48-hour window.

Deep-dive: 2028-03-08 at 10:00 PT works for our infra folks. Please include networking and any required VPC peering checklist.

Security note: before any POC we’ll need a one-pager on data residency and KMS integration.

—Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Engineering | Tidewell Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@tidewell.ai>; Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO bucketization + fallback playbook — quick technical addendum

Priya / Jordan — quick follow-up from the infra perspective. A couple of concrete suggestions we can bring to the deep-dive: 

- Continuous batching with dynamic batch-size caps: this will keep p95 low for short prompts while allowing throughput for long ones. We usually recommend a 20–40ms batch window for the short cohort.
- Prefix / KV cache: for templated replies we expect cache hit rates of 30–55% depending on prompt churn; I attached kv-cache-estimates.xlsx with a worked example showing token savings and expected p99 impact.
- Model variants: route short cohort to a 7B quantized profile on dedicated reserved capacity, long cohort to a 13B on mixed capacity (spot + reserved) with an automated fallback to the 3B cheap variant if queueing exceeds threshold.
- Fallback behavior: serve a shorter completion (truncate generation to 2x expected tokens) or return a cached templated response under severe overload.

Network/VPC notes: we’ll need your egress IPs or a peering config; Redwood supports private ingress via tunnel and a customer-controlled NAT for auditability. I’ll bring a checklist for VPC peering and KMS binding to the call.
